To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mutation in the FERM-domain of Jak3, a protein kinase involved in T, B and natural killer (NK) cell development, protects mice against the neurological complication of malaria known as cerebral malaria (CM).

we have used a genome-wide screen of a mouse mutagenesis library to identify a novel host factor (Jak3) that is required for the development of cerebral malaria in Plasmodium berghei ANKA-infected mice and that inhibition of Jak3 activity protects against cerebral malaria.
a dominant negative mutation in Jak3 protects mice from cerebral malaria, and this protection is dependent on the presence of normal CD8+ T-cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a dominant-negative mutation in Jak3 kinase that protects against lethal CM.
the identification and characterization of novel genetic factors involved in malaria pathogenesis.
the identification of host factors that are involved in the pathogenesis of cerebral malaria and that could be targeted by novel therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Jak3W81 is an essential gene for T cell development, but a dominant-negative variant of Jak3W82 is a novel host factor that protects against CM by inhibiting CD8+ T-cell responses and IFN-γ production.
Jak3W81 is the first ENU-induced mutation identified to confer CM resistance, and that the Jak3W81 mutant behaves as a dominant-negative variant.
Jak3 is a key host factor in the pathogenesis of cerebral malaria, and its inhibition is a potential therapeutic strategy for the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Jak3 is required for CD8+ T-cell function, and that Jak3W81 is a dominant negative allele, and therefore, a potential therapeutic target in CM.

the Jak3 kinase, which plays a key role in the development of T and B cells, is also critical for CD8+ T-cell-mediated Th1 responses and that a dominant negative Jak3 mutation protects against the neurological complications of malaria.
the Jak3W81 mutation is a dominant negative mutation that inhibits IFN-gamma production by CD8+ T lymphocytes and protects against cerebral malaria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single point mutation in Jak3, a key regulator of T cell development, can confer significant resistance against CM in mice.
the Jak3W81 mutation is a novel dominant negative allele that protects against CM.
a dominant negative mutation in Jak3, which is an important kinase involved in T cell activation and IFN-γ production, protects mice against lethal cerebral malaria.
